crossStoryFindings: AC-4 provenance behavior is inconsistent across the epic: `informed_work` is over-attributed to every current source, while `received_code_update` is unreachable on the default runtime path.

Detach/read/hydration stories are not fully aligned: detached attachments disappear from current-source views, but durable working-set state can still carry them forward into environment fingerprints.
architectureFindings: The runtime contract does not expose source-use signals, even though the tech design assigns source-use/code-update signaling to the tool runtime, so the provenance layer cannot distinguish "attached" from "actually used."
Working-set truth is split across current material refs, active-source resolution, and persisted environment fingerprints; detach only updates the attachment row, which creates cross-story drift.
epicCoverageAssessment: Focused Epic 6 suites pass when run directly: 78 server/convex tests and 20 client tests passed.
Attach/update/refresh/detach surfaces are broadly implemented, but the provenance guarantees still rely on test seams or inferred state instead of the real production default path.
`green-verify` and `verify-all` both fail before the epic suites run because Biome rejects the nested root configuration at `packages/lbuild-impl/biome.json`.
productionPathFindings: The default runtime still uses the placeholder execution payload, so the production path never emits code checkpoint candidates and cannot generate `received_code_update` provenance.
`createApp` still allows a story0/`NullPlatformStore` fallback in production after only a warning, leaving a non-real control-plane path available under misconfiguration.

blockingFindings.title: Informed-work provenance records every current source, not the sources actually used
blockingFindings.evidence: `ExecutionResult` has no source-use field (`apps/platform/server/services/processes/environment/provider-adapter.ts:125-131`). After every run, `ProcessEnvironmentService` unconditionally calls `recordInformedWorkForCurrentSources` (`apps/platform/server/services/processes/environment/process-environment.service.ts:565-568`), and `DefaultSourceProvenanceService` then writes one `informed_work` row per active current source (`apps/platform/server/services/sources/source-provenance.service.ts:48-76`). A run can therefore claim provenance for repositories the execution never touched.

blockingFindings.title: The default production execution path cannot produce received_code_update provenance
blockingFindings.evidence: `createApp` wires `new ScriptExecutionService(providerAdapterRegistry)` by default (`apps/platform/server/app.ts:266-267`). That service still ships the explicit placeholder payload (`apps/platform/server/services/processes/environment/script-execution.service.ts:9-68`), and the payload emits `codeCheckpointCandidates: []`. Normal runtime executions therefore cannot reach the code-write/provenance lane needed for `received_code_update` entries.

blockingFindings.title: Detach does not fully remove a source from durable working-set state
blockingFindings.evidence: `detachSourceAttachment` only stamps `detachedAt` on the source row (`convex/sourceAttachments.ts:279-317`). The persisted environment fingerprint still hashes every `currentSourceAttachmentId` without filtering detached rows (`convex/processEnvironmentStates.ts:245-290`), and `setProcessHydrationPlan` recomputes that fingerprint from the stale refs instead of from the filtered plan (`convex/processEnvironmentStates.ts:563-620`). Start/resume build hydration plans from `resolveActiveProcessSourceAttachments` (`apps/platform/server/services/processes/process-start.service.ts:57-78`), so later hydrations can exclude a detached source while the stored fingerprint still claims it is part of the working set.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Production bootstrap still tolerates the story0/NullPlatformStore fallback
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: `createApp` defaults to `story0PlaceholderEnv` and swaps in `NullPlatformStore` whenever `hasLiveConvexConfig` is false (`apps/platform/server/app.ts:171-185`; `apps/platform/server/config.ts:48-72`), then only logs a warning in production (`apps/platform/server/app.ts:205-208`). `NullPlatformStore` still returns synthetic process/source objects and placeholder repository identity in its source-management methods (`apps/platform/server/services/projects/platform-store.ts:912-1247`).

unresolvedItems: `corepack pnpm run green-verify` fails at `format:check` because Biome reports a nested root configuration in `packages/lbuild-impl/biome.json`.
`corepack pnpm run verify-all` fails for the same reason before integration/e2e phases start.

crossStoryFindings: The active-source resolver does not implement the Tech Design shadowing rule that pulls in a process-scoped sibling when it shadows an active project-scoped source but is not yet listed in current material refs, so materials reads, refresh targeting, hydration planning, and provenance enrichment can disagree on the canonical source.

Recoverable missing-working-copy handling is only modeled in docs/tests; no production path synthesizes `freshnessReason: working_copy_missing`, so source state can remain `hydrated` when the working copy is actually gone and the refresh flow never becomes available.

Story 4 provenance is wired end-to-end, but the real execution lane it depends on is still driven by the shared placeholder payload, so the epic’s cross-story provenance claims are only partially backed by real runtime behavior.
architectureFindings: `apps/platform/server/services/processes/active-process-sources.ts` drifts from Tech Design Question 7 / Active Source Resolution rule 5 by requiring the process-scoped row itself to already be current before it can shadow the project-scoped row.
`apps/platform/server/app.ts` still allows `NullPlatformStore` as a runtime fallback even though the architecture says Convex owns durable source attachment and provenance persistence.

The source-management APIs use real Fastify, Convex, GitHub, and provider seams when configured, but `ScriptExecutionService` remains a placeholder execution boundary, so canonical source provenance is not fully architecture-consistent on the production path.
epicCoverageAssessment: Attach/update/detach/provenance routes, Convex tables, shared contracts, and most Epic 6 automated coverage are present; targeted epic-specific runs passed for the source-management/provenance suite (80/80 tests in one batch, plus `process-materials-section` 4/4 under jsdom).
AC-3’s recoverable missing-working-copy path is not implemented end-to-end.
AC-4.2’s received-code-update provenance is not reachable through the default production execution payload because it never emits code checkpoint candidates.
Full epic gate validation could not complete because both required gate commands failed during the repo-wide Biome format check before the later test phases ran.
productionPathFindings: The default production server wiring still uses `buildDefaultScriptPayload()` through `new ScriptExecutionService(providerAdapterRegistry)`, and that payload hard-codes `codeCheckpointCandidates: []`, so `received_code_update` provenance is not produced by the real default execution path.
If live Convex config is absent, `createApp` falls back to `NullPlatformStore`, whose source-management methods return synthetic success payloads without durable persistence.
No production code path currently marks a hydrated source as `stale` with `freshnessReason: working_copy_missing`; the string only appears in a read-back branch, not in a state-producing path.

blockingFindings.title: Default execution payload makes received-code-update provenance unreachable
blockingFindings.evidence: `apps/platform/server/services/processes/environment/script-execution.service.ts` wires `buildDefaultScriptPayload()` by default, and that payload hard-codes `codeCheckpointCandidates: []`. `apps/platform/server/app.ts` constructs `new ScriptExecutionService(providerAdapterRegistry)` without overriding the factory. A direct `tsx` check printed `codeCheckpointCandidates empty`, so the default real runtime never produces code checkpoint candidates for `recordReceivedCodeUpdates` to persist.

blockingFindings.title: Recoverable missing working copies never transition into the required stale source state
blockingFindings.evidence: The only non-test production occurrence of `working_copy_missing` is the guard in `apps/platform/server/services/sources/source-refresh.service.ts`; there is no production code that sets that freshness reason. `synchronizeProjectSourceAttachments` evaluates GitHub repository state only, not environment/working-copy state, so a missing hydrated working copy cannot become the required recoverable `stale` condition.

blockingFindings.title: Active-source resolver misses the design’s process-shadow sibling rule
blockingFindings.evidence: Tech Design Active Source Resolution rule 5 says a process-scoped sibling with the same `repositoryFullName + targetRef` must shadow an active project-scoped row even when its own id is not yet in `currentSourceAttachmentIds`. `apps/platform/server/services/processes/active-process-sources.ts` only includes process-scoped rows whose ids are current. A direct `tsx` evaluation with current ids set to `['project-1']` returned the project row instead of the matching process-scoped shadow.

blockingFindings.title: Required verification gates fail before epic validation can complete
blockingFindings.evidence: `corepack pnpm run green-verify` and `corepack pnpm run verify-all` both fail in `format:check` with Biome reporting `Found a nested root configuration` for `packages/lbuild-impl/biome.json`, so the required story/epic gates do not currently pass.

blockingFindings.title: Source-management can silently succeed against a fake non-durable store when Convex is missing
blockingFindings.evidence: `apps/platform/server/app.ts` falls back to `new NullPlatformStore()` when live Convex config is absent. In `apps/platform/server/services/projects/platform-store.ts`, `NullPlatformStore.createProjectSourceAttachment` returns a synthetic summary while `listProjectSourceAttachments` always returns `[]`. A direct `tsx` create-then-list check returned a created attachment with `listedCount: 0`, proving the fallback is non-real and non-durable.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Automated coverage does not pin the missing shadow-sibling case
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: The Epic 6 source-management test suite covers shadowing when both the project-scoped row and the process shadow are already current, but I found no test that asserts the Tech Design rule where only the project-scoped id is current and the process-scoped sibling must still shadow it.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Automated coverage models working-copy-missing as fixture input rather than a produced runtime state
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: Epic tests and fixtures assert that `working_copy_missing` renders correctly when pre-seeded, but I did not find a runtime test that proves environment loss or missing working-copy recovery actually produces that source state from live server behavior.

unresolvedItems: Decide whether the platform should fail fast when Convex is unavailable or explicitly expose a read-only/unavailable source-management mode; the current `NullPlatformStore` fallback silently fabricates success responses.

Decide whether Epic 6 is allowed to ship while the default execution lane is still the shared placeholder payload, because AC-4.2 currently depends on follow-on execution work that has not landed on the real runtime path.
